About

About Me

My name is Parth Patel, and I am an entry-level cybersecurity and IT professional preparing for a career as a Cybersecurity Analyst. I am currently a senior at Houston Community College, where I am pursuing an Associate in Applied Science in Computer Systems Networking.

I have gained experience through cybersecurity coursework, NCL/Cyber Skyline participation, XP Cyber Range Challenges, NDG Guided Labs, Cybersecurity Operations project challenges, certifications, and independent technical projects.

I am not currently involved in college clubs or organizations, but I continue building my cybersecurity experience through coursework, labs, competitions, certifications, and independent learning.

Role Model

A cybersecurity role model I look up to is Kevin Mitnick because of his focus on social engineering, security awareness, and the human side of security.

“Companies spend millions of dollars on firewalls, encryption and secure access devices, and it’s money wasted because none of these measures address the weakest link in the security chain.”

This quote reminds me that cybersecurity is not only about tools. People, awareness, procedures, and decision-making are also important parts of security.

Featured Projects

Scout AI – Competitive Intelligence Website

Website: https://scout-ai-taupe.vercel.app/

Scout AI is an AI-powered competitive intelligence website that generates structured market research, competitor analysis, risks, opportunities, and executive-style summaries from a single prompt. The project allows a user to enter a company name, optional website, and research goal, then produces a competitive brief with an executive takeaway, company summary, competitor analysis, strengths, weaknesses, and positioning insights.

Cybersecurity connection: This project connects to cybersecurity because analysts often gather information, organize findings, compare data, and write clear reports. The project helped me practice OSINT-style research, data handling, report writing, and web application awareness.

Security Log Analysis & Incident Reporting

This Cybersecurity Operations project challenge focused on reviewing simulated security events using SIEM and SOC concepts. The goal was to identify suspicious activity, analyze evidence, document a timeline, and create an incident-style report with recommended response steps.

SIEM ConceptsLog AnalysisIncident Reporting

I learned that small details such as timestamps, usernames, IP addresses, repeated actions, and unusual behavior can help determine whether an event is suspicious.

Vulnerability Assessment & Risk Prioritization

This Cybersecurity Operations project challenge focused on identifying vulnerabilities, understanding severity, applying CVSS scoring, and prioritizing remediation based on risk.

Vulnerability AssessmentCVSSRisk Prioritization

I learned that vulnerability management requires ranking risk, explaining impact, and recommending practical fixes in a clear way.

Reflection

Reflections & Lessons Learned

Throughout this course and my hands-on cybersecurity activities, I gained a better understanding of what cybersecurity professionals do in real-world environments. Before completing these projects and labs, I mostly thought of cybersecurity as protecting computers and networks from hackers. Now, I understand that cybersecurity includes monitoring systems, analyzing logs, identifying vulnerabilities, documenting incidents, assessing risk, and communicating findings clearly.

One of the biggest skills I gained was security analysis. Through SIEM/log review and incident reporting activities, I learned how to look at security events carefully and search for evidence. I learned that small details such as timestamps, usernames, IP addresses, repeated login attempts, unusual behavior, and system alerts can help determine whether an event is suspicious.

Another important skill I gained was vulnerability prioritization. In vulnerability assessment work, I learned that not every vulnerability has the same level of risk. Learning about CVSS scoring and remediation planning helped me understand how cybersecurity teams decide what to fix first.

One challenge I encountered was working through technical tasks when I did not immediately know the answer. Some labs and challenges required me to slow down, reread instructions, research unfamiliar terms, and test different approaches. This helped me build persistence and improve my technical confidence.

Overall, this course helped me grow by giving me hands-on practice, exposure to cybersecurity tools and concepts, and a better understanding of the skills needed in the field. I plan to continue learning through certifications, labs, projects, and practical experience.
